newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end higher, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end higher, seen falling.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished slightly higher on Friday as the banking system continued to show a negative reserve excess following recent mop-up measures by the central bank, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.500 against Thursday's 6.477 close -- well above the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent -- with 30-day commercial paper at 6.50-6.80 against 6.50-6.75.

Dealers expected the overnight rate to drop to around 6.25 percent level next week as the central bank's previous issues of the negotiable certificates of deposit worth T$17 billion are due to mature.
Funds that flowed out of the banking system in early June also would return gradually to ease liquidity.
In the bond market, the benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield was expected to stay in range trading next week. Short-term interest rate movement will remain a key focus, dealers said.
